deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1953 functional-analysis notes on topological exterior powers. The material feeds into his Fredholm theory (Fredholm determinants and the eigenvalue estimates in 'La théorie de Fredholm', Bull. SMF 1956, and the Fredholm part of the PTT thesis).

(1) The first lines finish the Hilbert-space case of an earlier section. The norm on the completed exterior power \hat\Lambda^n E is the Hilbert norm given by Gram determinants, (a_1∧…∧a_n, b_1∧…∧b_n) = det((a_i,b_j)). Cauchy–Schwarz, together with the orthonormal basis e_J of \hat\Lambda^n E from the previous page, shows that all comparison constants of Chap. I §2 n°2 can be taken equal to 1. Those constants compare the norms on Λ^n of the dual with the dual of Λ^n, the dual E' being identified with the conjugate space \bar E.

(2) Now let E, F be Hilbert spaces and u_1,…,u_n ∈ L(E,F). Their exterior product u_1∧…∧u_n (Chap. I §1 n°1) is the polarized form of Λ^n u, so that u∧…∧u = Λ^n u. Formula (8) factors it as
  u_1∧…∧u_n = φ_n ∘ (u_1⊗…⊗u_n) ∘ a_n,
where:
- a_n : \hat\Lambda^n E → \hat⊗^n E is the canonical antisymmetrizing injection;
- φ_n : \hat⊗^n F → \hat\Lambda^n F is the canonical quotient map.
With the Gram-determinant inner product, a_n/√(n!) is an isometry and √(n!)·φ_n has norm ≤ 1. This is consistent provided φ_n∘a_n = id, i.e. φ_n carries the factor 1/n!. The Hilbert tensor norm is a cross norm on operators: ||u_1⊗…⊗u_n|| = Π||u_i||. Hence
  (9) ||u_1∧…∧u_n|| ≤ ||u_1||…||u_n||.
In particular ||Λ^n u|| ≤ ||u||^n.

(3) Consequently u_1∧…∧u_n extends by continuity to a bounded map \hat\Lambda^n E → \hat\Lambda^n F, still written the same way, and the usual algebraic rules persist. The next page adds functoriality Λ(vu) = Λv Λu, compatibility with adjoints (Λu)* = Λ(u*), positivity, and (Λh)^α = Λ(h^α).

The purpose is the standard machinery behind Fredholm determinants and Weyl-type inequalities: ||Λ^n u|| equals the product of the top n singular values.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. The stated normalizations (a_n/√n! an isometry, √n!·φ_n a contraction, and (8) with no 1/n! factor) are mutually consistent only if φ_n(x_1⊗…⊗x_n) = (1/n!)·x_1∧…∧x_n, so that φ_n∘a_n = id. With the other common convention one needs a factor n! in (8) and the roles of the √n! scalings change. Inequality (9) is correct in any case.

ideas.what: Hilbert exterior power with Gram-determinant inner product; comparison constants equal to 1 in the Hilbert case
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert-space exterior power / antisymmetric Fock space component
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Grassmann, Weyl); standard in operator theory
ideas.where_published: La théorie de Fredholm (Bull. SMF 1956); Produits tensoriels topologiques (Memoirs AMS 1955)

ideas.what: Factorization of u_1∧…∧u_n through tensor powers and the bound ||u_1∧…∧u_n|| ≤ Π||u_i||
ideas.modern_name: Norm of the exterior power of operators, ||Λ^n u|| ≤ ||u||^n (mixed version)

ideas.what: Extension by continuity to completed exterior powers, with the usual calculus preserved
ideas.modern_name: Functor Λ^n on bounded operators between Hilbert spaces

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine preliminaries (Hilbert exterior powers and the norm bound for exterior products of operators) leading to Grothendieck's published Fredholm theory. There is nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 's'imaginer l'inégalité de Cauchy-Schwarz' is likely 'd'appliquer l'inégalité de Cauchy-Schwarz'.
'√n! φ_n une norme de norme ≤ 1' should read 'une application (homomorphisme) de norme ≤ 1'.
'Comme 1/√n! a_n est une isométrie de [...]' should read 'une isométrie de \hat\Lambda E dans \hat⊗E'.
'en vertu de (4)' is uncertain; the image suggests '(7)' or '(d)', i.e. the cross-norm property ||u_1⊗…⊗u_n|| = Π||u_i||.
'les constantes [?]' is plausibly correct: the constants of Chap. I §2 N°2.
